chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, from Muyassar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

O Muyassar, what is the distance between you and Qarqaysa? I said, 'It is near, on the bank of the Euphrates.' He said, 'Indeed, there will be a battle/clash at it, the like of which has not occurred since Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created the heavens and the earth, nor will the like of it occur as long as the heavens and the earth remain. It will be a banquet for the birds; the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky will be satisfied from it. Qays will be destroyed in it, and no one will call for a helper for it.'
He said, 'And not one person has narrated it, and he added to it: And a caller will call out,

key_terms.قِرْقِيسَا: Qarqaysa, a location on the Euphrates

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the battle at Qarqaysa mentioned in the hadith of Abu Ja'far?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the eschatological significance of Qarqaysa, a location on the Euphrates, as the site of a cataclysmic battle foretold by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) involving the destruction of the Qays tribe. The vivid imagery of the earth becoming a 'banquet' for birds and beasts underscores the magnitude of the conflict, while the additional narration of the caller inviting people to the 'meat of the tyrants' emphasizes the decisive defeat of oppressive forces, a theme often linked to the final victory of the Mahdi (AJTFS) in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali: H 14899 – Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzaal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from his father, from Muyassar, who has narrated the following: Abu Ja’farasws has said:

‘O Muyassar, how much distance is there in between you and Qarqaysa?’ I said, ‘It is near to the banks of the Euphrates’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, there will transpire an event with it, the like of which has never happened since Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created the Heavens and the earth, nor will the like of it happen so long as the Heavens and the earth remain. It will be a banquet for the birds. The lions of the earth and the birds of the skies would satisfy their hunger. Qays would be killed in it and there will be no helper called for him’.
(The narrator) said, ‘And someone else has reported an addition to it: ‘And a caller will call out, ‘Come to the meat of the tyrants!’
en.sarwar: 452. From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al-Husayn Bin Saeed, from Hammaad Bin Isa, from Al-Husayn Bin Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said: ‘
Every banner rose before the rising of Al-Qaim (a.s.), so its owner is a tyrant who worships someone apart from Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic’.
